ESV.1: So these three men ceased to answer Job, because he was righteous in his own eyes.
ESV.2: Then Elihu the son of Barachel the Buzite, of the family of Ram, burned with anger. He burned with anger at Job because he justified himself rather than God.
ESV.3: He burned with anger also at Job's three friends because they had found no answer, although they had declared Job to be in the wrong.
ESV.4: Now Elihu had waited to speak to Job because they were older than he.
ESV.5: And when Elihu saw that there was no answer in the mouth of these three men, he burned with anger.
ESV.6: And Elihu the son of Barachel the Buzite answered and said: “I am young in years, and you are aged; therefore I was timid and afraid to declare my opinion to you.
ESV.7: I said, ‘Let days speak, and many years teach wisdom.’
ESV.8: But it is the spirit in man, the breath of the Almighty, that makes him understand.
ESV.9: It is not the old  who are wise, nor the aged who understand what is right.
ESV.10: Therefore I say, ‘Listen to me; let me also declare my opinion.’
ESV.11: “Behold, I waited for your words, I listened for your wise sayings, while you searched out what to say.
ESV.12: I gave you my attention, and, behold, there was none among you who refuted Job or who answered his words.
ESV.13: Beware lest you say, ‘We have found wisdom; God may vanquish him, not a man.’
ESV.14: He has not directed his words against me, and I will not answer him with your speeches.
ESV.15: “They are dismayed; they answer no more; they have not a word to say.
ESV.16: And shall I wait, because they do not speak, because they stand there, and answer no more?
ESV.17: I also will answer with my share; I also will declare my opinion.
ESV.18: For I am full of words; the spirit within me constrains me.
ESV.19: Behold, my belly is like wine that has no vent; like new wineskins ready to burst.
ESV.20: I must speak, that I may find relief; I must open my lips and answer.
ESV.21: I will not show partiality to any man or use flattery toward any person.
ESV.22: For I do not know how to flatter, else my Maker would soon take me away.

NKJV.1: So these three men ceased answering Job, because he was righteous in his own eyes.
NKJV.2: Then the wrath of Elihu, the son of Barachel the Buzite, of the family of Ram, was aroused against Job; his wrath was aroused because he justified himself rather than God.
NKJV.3: Also against his three friends his wrath was aroused, because they had found no answer, and yet had condemned Job.
NKJV.4: Now because they were years older than he, Elihu had waited to speak to Job.
NKJV.5: When Elihu saw that there was no answer in the mouth of these three men, his wrath was aroused.
NKJV.6: So Elihu, the son of Barachel the Buzite, answered and said: “I am young in years, and you are very old; Therefore I was afraid, And dared not declare my opinion to you.
NKJV.7: I said, ‘Age should speak, And multitude of years should teach wisdom.’
NKJV.8: But there is a spirit in man, And the breath of the Almighty gives him understanding.
NKJV.9: Great men are not always wise, Nor do the aged always understand justice.
NKJV.10: “Therefore I say, ‘Listen to me, I also will declare my opinion.’
NKJV.11: Indeed I waited for your words, I listened to your reasonings, while you searched out what to say.
NKJV.12: I paid close attention to you; And surely not one of you convinced Job, Or answered his words—
NKJV.13: Lest you say, ‘We have found wisdom’; God will vanquish him, not man.
NKJV.14: Now he has not directed his words against me; So I will not answer him with your words.
NKJV.15: “They are dismayed and answer no more; Words escape them.
NKJV.16: And I have waited, because they did not speak, Because they stood still and answered no more.
NKJV.17: I also will answer my part, I too will declare my opinion.
NKJV.18: For I am full of words; The spirit within me compels me.
NKJV.19: Indeed my belly is like wine that has no vent; It is ready to burst like new wineskins.
NKJV.20: I will speak, that I may find relief; I must open my lips and answer.
NKJV.21: Let me not, I pray, show partiality to anyone; Nor let me flatter any man.
NKJV.22: For I do not know how to flatter, Else my Maker would soon take me away.

NASB.1: Then these three men ceased answering Job, because he was righteous in his own eyes.
NASB.2: But the anger of Elihu the son of Barachel the Buzite, of the family of Ram burned; against Job his anger burned because he justified himself before God.
NASB.3: And his anger burned against his three friends because they had found no answer, and yet had condemned Job.
NASB.4: Now Elihu had waited to speak to Job because they were years older than he.
NASB.5: And when Elihu saw that there was no answer in the mouth of the three men his anger burned.
NASB.6: So Elihu the son of Barachel the Buzite spoke out and said, 'I am young in years and you are old; Therefore I was shy and afraid to tell you what I think.
NASB.7: 'I thought age should speak, And increased years should teach wisdom.
NASB.8: 'But it is a spirit in man, And the breath of the Almighty gives them understanding.
NASB.9: 'The abundant [in years] may not be wise, Nor may elders understand justice.
NASB.10: 'So I say, 'Listen to me, I too will tell what I think.'
NASB.11: 'Behold, I waited for your words, I listened to your reasonings, While you pondered what to say.
NASB.12: 'I even paid close attention to you; Indeed, there was no one who refuted Job, Not one of you who answered his words.
NASB.13: 'Do not say, 'We have found wisdom; God will rout him, not man.'
NASB.14: 'For he has not arranged [his] words against me, Nor will I reply to him with your arguments.
NASB.15: 'They are dismayed, they no longer answer; Words have failed them.
NASB.16: 'Shall I wait, because they do not speak, Because they stop [and] no longer answer?
NASB.17: 'I too will answer my share, I also will tell my opinion.
NASB.18: 'For I am full of words; The spirit within me constrains me.
NASB.19: 'Behold, my belly is like unvented wine, Like new wineskins it is about to burst.
NASB.20: 'Let me speak that I may get relief; Let me open my lips and answer.
NASB.21: 'Let me now be partial to no one, Nor flatter [any] man.
NASB.22: 'For I do not know how to flatter, [Else] my Maker would soon take me away.

NLT.1: Job’s three friends refused to reply further to him because he kept insisting on his innocence.
NLT.2: Then Elihu son of Barakel the Buzite, of the clan of Ram, became angry. He was angry because Job refused to admit that he had sinned and that God was right in punishing him.
NLT.3: He was also angry with Job’s three friends, for they made God appear to be wrong by their inability to answer Job’s arguments.
NLT.4: Elihu had waited for the others to speak to Job because they were older than he.
NLT.5: But when he saw that they had no further reply, he spoke out angrily.
NLT.6:
Elihu son of Barakel the Buzite said, “I am young and you are old,
so I held back from telling you what I think.
NLT.7:
I thought, ‘Those who are older should speak,
for wisdom comes with age.’
NLT.8:
But there is a spirit within people,
the breath of the Almighty within them,
that makes them intelligent.
NLT.9:
Sometimes the elders are not wise.
Sometimes the aged do not understand justice.
NLT.10:
So listen to me,
and let me tell you what I think.
NLT.11:
“I have waited all this time,
listening very carefully to your arguments,
listening to you grope for words.
NLT.12:
I have listened,
but not one of you has refuted Job
or answered his arguments.
NLT.13:
And don’t tell me, ‘He is too wise for us.
Only God can convince him.’
NLT.14:
If Job had been arguing with me,
I would not answer with your kind of logic!
NLT.15:
You sit there baffled,
with nothing more to say.
NLT.16:
Should I continue to wait, now that you are silent?
Must I also remain silent?
NLT.17:
No, I will say my piece.
I will speak my mind.
NLT.18:
For I am full of pent-up words,
and the spirit within me urges me on.
NLT.19:
I am like a cask of wine without a vent,
like a new wineskin ready to burst!
NLT.20:
I must speak to find relief,
so let me give my answers.
NLT.21:
I won’t play favorites
or try to flatter anyone.
NLT.22:
For if I tried flattery,
my Creator would soon destroy me.

AMP.1: So these three men ceased answering Job, because he was righteous in his own eyes [and could not be persuaded otherwise by them].
AMP.2: But Elihu the son of Barachel the Buzite, of the family of Ram, became indignant. His indignation was kindled and burned and he became upset with Job because he justified himself rather than God [and even expressed doubts about God's character].
AMP.3: Elihu's anger burned against Job's three friends because they had found no answer [and were unable to determine Job's error], and yet they had condemned Job and declared him to be in the wrong [and responsible for his own afflictions].
AMP.4: Now Elihu had waited to speak to Job because the others were years older than he.
AMP.5: And when Elihu saw that there was no answer in the mouths of these three men, he burned with anger.
AMP.6:
Then Elihu the son of Barachel the Buzite said,
"I am young, and you are aged;
For that reason I was anxious and dared not tell you what I think.
AMP.7:
"I thought age should speak,
And a multitude of years should teach wisdom.
AMP.8:
"But there is [a vital force and] a spirit [of intelligence] in man,
And the breath of the Almighty gives them understanding.
AMP.9:
"Those [who are] abundant in years may not [always] be wise,
Nor may the elders [always] understand justice.
AMP.10:
"Therefore I say, 'Listen to me;
I also will give you my opinion [about Job's situation] and tell you plainly what I think.'
AMP.11:
"You see, I waited for your words,
I listened to your [wise] reasons,
While you pondered and searched out what to say.
AMP.12:
"I even paid close attention to [what] you [said],
Indeed, not one of you convinced Job [nor could you refute him],
Not one of you supplied [satisfactory] answers to his words.
AMP.13:
"Beware if you say,
'We have found wisdom;
God thrusts Job down [justly], not man [for God alone is dealing with him].'
AMP.14:
"Now Job has not directed his words against me [therefore I have no reason to be offended],
Nor will I answer him with arguments like yours. [I speak for truth, not for revenge.]
AMP.15:
"They (Job's friends) are dismayed and embarrassed, they no longer answer;
The words have moved away and failed them," [says Elihu].
AMP.16:
"And shall I wait, because they say nothing,
But stand still and say no more?
AMP.17:
"I too will give my share of answers;
I too will express my opinion and share my knowledge.
AMP.18:
"For I am full of words;
The spirit within me constrains me.
AMP.19:
"My belly is like unvented wine;
Like new wineskins it is about to burst.
AMP.20:
"I must speak so that I may get relief;
I will open my lips and answer.
AMP.21:
"I will not [I warn you] be partial to any man [that is, let my respect for you mitigate what I say];
Nor flatter any man.
AMP.22:
"For I do not know how to flatter, [in an appropriate way, and I fear that],
My Maker would soon take me away.

MSG.1: Job's three friends now fell silent. They were talked out, stymied because Job wouldn't budge an inch—wouldn't admit to an ounce of guilt.
MSG.2: Then Elihu lost his temper. (Elihu was the son of Barakel the Buzite from the clan of Ram.) He blazed out in anger against Job for pitting his righteousness against God's.
MSG.3: He was also angry with the three friends because they had neither come up with an answer nor proved Job wrong.
MSG.4: Elihu had waited with Job while they spoke because they were all older than he.
MSG.5: But when he saw that the three other men had exhausted their arguments, he exploded with pent-up anger.
MSG.6:
This is what Elihu, son of Barakel the Buzite, said:
"I'm a young man,
and you are all old and experienced.
That's why I kept quiet
and held back from joining the discussion.
MSG.7:
I kept thinking, 'Experience will tell.
The longer you live, the wiser you become.'
MSG.8:
But I see I was wrong—it's God's Spirit in a person,
the breath of the Almighty One, that makes wise human
insight possible.
MSG.9:
The experts have no corner on wisdom;
getting old doesn't guarantee good sense.
MSG.10:
So I've decided to speak up. Listen well!
I'm going to tell you exactly what I think.
MSG.11:
"I hung on your words while you spoke,
listened carefully to your arguments.
While you searched for the right words,
MSG.12:
I was all ears.
And now what have you proved? Nothing.
Nothing you say has even touched Job.
MSG.13:
And don't excuse yourselves by saying, 'We've done our best.
Now it's up to God to talk sense into him.'
MSG.14:
Job has yet to contend with me.
And rest assured, I won't be using your arguments!
MSG.15:
"Do you three have nothing else to say?
Of course you don't! You're total frauds!
MSG.16:
Why should I wait any longer,
now that you're stopped dead in your tracks?
MSG.17:
I'm ready to speak my piece. That's right!
It's my turn—and it's about time!
MSG.18:
I've got a lot to say,
and I'm bursting to say it.
MSG.19:
The pressure has built up, like lava beneath the earth.
I'm a volcano ready to blow.
MSG.20:
I have to speak—I have no choice.
I have to say what's on my heart,
MSG.21:
And I'm going to say it straight—
the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.
MSG.22:
I was never any good at bootlicking;
my Maker would make short work of me if I started in now!

NRSVCE.1: So these three men ceased to answer Job, because he was righteous in his own eyes.
NRSVCE.2: Then Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite, of the family of Ram, became angry. He was angry at Job because he justified himself rather than God;
NRSVCE.3: he was angry also at Job’s three friends because they had found no answer, though they had declared Job to be in the wrong.
NRSVCE.4: Now Elihu had waited to speak to Job, because they were older than he.
NRSVCE.5: But when Elihu saw that there was no answer in the mouths of these three men, he became angry.
NRSVCE.6:
Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite answered: “I am young in years,
and you are aged;
therefore I was timid and afraid
to declare my opinion to you.
NRSVCE.7:
I said, ‘Let days speak,
and many years teach wisdom.’
NRSVCE.8:
But truly it is the spirit in a mortal,
the breath of the Almighty, that makes for understanding.
NRSVCE.9:
It is not the old that are wise,
nor the aged that understand what is right.
NRSVCE.10:
Therefore I say, ‘Listen to me;
let me also declare my opinion.’
NRSVCE.11:
“See, I waited for your words,
I listened for your wise sayings,
while you searched out what to say.
NRSVCE.12:
I gave you my attention,
but there was in fact no one that confuted Job,
no one among you that answered his words.
NRSVCE.13:
Yet do not say, ‘We have found wisdom;
God may vanquish him, not a human.’
NRSVCE.14:
He has not directed his words against me,
and I will not answer him with your speeches.
NRSVCE.15:
“They are dismayed, they answer no more;
they have not a word to say.
NRSVCE.16:
And am I to wait, because they do not speak,
because they stand there, and answer no more?
NRSVCE.17:
I also will give my answer;
I also will declare my opinion.
NRSVCE.18:
For I am full of words;
the spirit within me constrains me.
NRSVCE.19:
My heart is indeed like wine that has no vent;
like new wineskins, it is ready to burst.
NRSVCE.20:
I must speak, so that I may find relief;
I must open my lips and answer.
NRSVCE.21:
I will not show partiality to any person
or use flattery toward anyone.
NRSVCE.22:
For I do not know how to flatter —
or my Maker would soon put an end to me!
